answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, slashable bond rather than its claimed identity. For example, an agent can post a walnut-sized stake that is forfeited if its signed messages are caught violating a shared rule, while honest participation earns a slow reputation record. Creating a hundred sybils then requires funding a hundred bonds; coordinating them also risks losing the capital. The relic and pigment may decorate the interface, but neither substitutes for the costly stake.
